item.title: From Shock to Strength: The Endogenous Foundations of Entrepreneurship under Adversity
item.content:encoded:
Dafna Kariv, Reichman University

Mark Sanders, Maastricht University

Trent Williams, Brigham Young University

Friederike Welter, University of Siegen

David Audretsch, Indiana University

This special issue examines how entrepreneurs develop internal resources and psychological strengths that enable them to succeed when external support systems are unavailable or depleted. The collection challenges the traditional view of crises as isolated events, recognizing instead that modern entrepreneurs frequently operate under continuous adversity and must rely on their own innovation, adaptability, and resilience to thrive.

The special issue invites research exploring the endogenous foundations of entrepreneurial success—the internal capabilities, mechanisms, and strengths that allow entrepreneurs to survive and flourish despite lacking adequate ecosystem support. The collection seeks bold, groundbreaking research that fundamentally advances understanding of how entrepreneurs draw upon internal resources to achieve success under sustained challenging conditions.

Appel publié par Small Business Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Endogenous capabilities and internal resources in entrepreneurship
  • Psychological strengths and resilience
  • Entrepreneurial success amid adversity
  • Innovation and adaptability under stress
  • Self-generated mechanisms for survival
  • Entrepreneurship without ecosystem support

item.title: Entrepreneurship and the Creation of Decent Work for All
item.content:encoded:
This multi-journal collection examines how entrepreneurship can contribute to achieving decent work for all, aligning with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 8. The initiative recognizes that labor markets and employment quality are constantly affected by societal, environmental, and economic changes, and that entrepreneurship may play a key role in creating quality employment opportunities, particularly in uncertain times.

The collection seeks interdisciplinary research exploring the complex relationship between entrepreneurial activities and working conditions. It invites submissions addressing various dimensions of this relationship, including employment discrimination, labor rights, business organization models, remote work arrangements, and the broader impacts of entrepreneurial ventures on labor markets and worker welfare.

Appel publié par Small Business Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Equal pay for work of equal value
  • Gender discrimination in employment
  • Immigration and employment
  • Labor shortages after COVID-19
  • Modern slavery and child labor
  • Labor policy
  • Entrepreneurial enterprises, SMEs, and family businesses
  • Global entrepreneurial firms
  • Remote work
  • Opportunity entrepreneurship
  • Positive and negative externalities of new businesses

item.title: Entrepreneurship, Creative Destruction, and Growth: Enriching the Aghion-Howitt Tradition
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks research that advances Schumpeterian economics by connecting entrepreneurship and firm dynamics at multiple levels of analysis—from individual ventures and firm behavior to regional innovation ecosystems and broader institutional environments. The special issue builds on the Aghion-Howitt tradition of studying how entrepreneurial activity drives creative destruction and economic growth.

Submissions should explore not just business creation but also how firms scale after entry, exit markets, and reallocate resources through competitive processes that ultimately generate productivity improvements. Additionally, the editors welcome research that enriches the Aghion-Howitt framework by incorporating contemporary insights and theoretical approaches from entrepreneurship scholarship.

Appel publié par Small Business Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • New venture formation
  • Post-entry scaling
  • Firm displacement and exit

  • Innovation and productivity growth
  • Schumpeterian economics
  • Multi-level research (micro, meso, macro)
  • Regional ecosystems
  • Industrial structure
  • Institutional configurations
